column1: # Corpus programs whose output depends on a check that `-O3` or `-O4` drops
# Columns (tab-separated): lowest level that drops the check, program,
# the check, what the program does with it. Reviewed by hand: each entry
# was confirmed to diverge only because of that check.

column4: `List<num>.add(2.5)` on a `List<int>`: the covariant parameter of `JSArray.add` no longer throws `TypeError`, and the double stays in the list
`int x = d` with `dynamic d = 'texto'` no longer throws `TypeError` (at -O4 its index cases no longer throw `RangeError` either)
`s1 + a` with dynamic `s1` a `String` and `a` an `int`: `String.+` no longer checks its argument, and JavaScript concatenates
`final String u = e ?? 'z'` with `dynamic e = 5` no longer throws `TypeError`
`nums.add(1.5)` through `List<num>` on a `List<int>` no longer throws `TypeError`; the program then fails on the double it kept
every line tests a covariant parameter or field (generic, `covariant`, overridden) that no longer throws `TypeError`
`c.n = 1.5` through the covariant `late` field of a supertype no longer throws `TypeError`
the covariance stubs and checked tear-offs it calls with wrong arguments no longer throw `TypeError`
dynamic values assigned to typed parameters, locals and record fields are accepted instead of throwing `TypeError`
`E<String>(value)` with `dynamic value = 0`: the forwarded constructor's argument is no longer checked
spreads, `for-in` and `await` of dynamic values of the wrong type no longer throw `TypeError`
the tear-off `c.foo` of a `C<int>` seen as `C<Object>`, assigned to `void Function(String)`, is no longer checked against its static type
the type arguments of dynamic generic calls are no longer checked against their bounds
a generic forwarder's covariant parameter accepts a value of the wrong type
a covariant setter accepts a value of the wrong type
dynamic values assigned to record fields and to `Never` are no longer checked
`l[10]` on a three-element list returns `undefined` instead of throwing `RangeError` (dart2js -O4 keeps this check: its inference does not prove the receiver a `JSArray`)
`[1][5]` no longer throws `RangeError`
`u8b[10]` on a five-element `Uint8List` no longer throws `RangeError` (dart2js -O4 keeps this check: `J.$index$ax`, its inference does not prove the receiver a native typed array)
`'abc'.codeUnitAt(3)` returns `NaN` instead of throwing `RangeError`
